name: Ransomware
description: Mass file encryption or deletion, shadow copy and backup removal, and ransom notes written to disk.

name: Credential theft
description: Access to LSASS memory, credential dumping tools, and harvesting of stored or cached credentials.

name: Malicious scripts
description: Obfuscated or encoded PowerShell, script hosts launched from Office or browsers, and abuse of built-in Windows binaries (LOLBins).

name: Defender tampering
description: Attempts to disable Microsoft Defender protection, add exclusions or stop security services.

name: Lateral movement
description: Remote execution, remote service creation and admin-share access from one device to another.

name: Known malware
description: Files and processes that Microsoft Defender Antivirus or threat intelligence identifies as known malware.

name: Persistence
description: Mechanisms that survive a restart: Run keys, Startup items, scheduled tasks, services, WMI event subscriptions and accessibility-feature hijacks.

name: Rogue administrator account
description: New local or domain accounts, and accounts added to privileged groups outside the normal process.

name: Discovery
description: Bursts of reconnaissance commands that enumerate users, groups, shares, hosts and network configuration.

name: Data exfiltration
description: Staging and archiving of data followed by unusual outbound transfers, including slow transfers spread over time.

name: Command and control
description: Periodic beaconing, named pipes used by attack frameworks, and programs that normally never connect to the internet doing so.

name: Exploited vulnerability
description: A device with a Critical or High vulnerability that has a public exploit, combined with signs of exploitation or other attack behaviour on the same device.
